newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico blue chips end up on Telmex earnings hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico blue chips end up on Telmex earnings hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed mixed but blue chips were up for the second day in a row on Thursday amid selective buying by bargain hunters.
"Trading volume was mediocre today. Dealers bought on the expectation that Telmex's earnings would be good. Relative stability in the dollar allowed people to focus on earnings again," said a trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 14.67 points, or 0.45 percent, at 3,279.21. Telmex earnings were due to be released after the close of trade on Thursday.

Telmex, the heaviest weighted company included in the IPC, closed up 16 centavos (2 cents) at 12.44 pesos ($1.58), and its ADRs shunned the sliding Dow Jones industrial average in New York to end up 1/4 at 31-1/2 as investors bought up the stock before the announcement.
Volume was lackluster at 64.8 million shares traded and on the broad market scoreboard, losers outnumbered gainers by 48 to 36, out of 111 shares traded.

Autoparts maker Iasasa A and B series shares headed the percentage leaders, both closing up six centavos (1 cent) at 50 centavos (6 cents). Traders said the share was edging up towards a target price of 60 centavos.
Pharmaceutical firm Autrey came in third place, up 58 centavos (7 cents) to 15.18 pesos ($1.93), after reporting during the session.
Although not among percentage gain leaders, several other stocks ended up after reporting earnings on Thursday.

Holding company Alfa closed up 40 centavos (5 cents) at 34.00 pesos ($4.32), cement firm Apasco was up 50 centavos (6 cents) at 50.50 pesos ($6.41), and steelmakers Hylsamex gained 50 centavos (6 cents) to 29.50 pesos ($3.75).

Financial stock GFInver dominated the loss leaders, meanwhile, following an announcement the group was to be taken over by Spanish-based Banco Santander. A trader said the market was "selling on the news after buying on the rumour."

GFInver BCP, LCP, ACP and CCP series shares closed down 32 (4 cents), 20 centavos (3 cents), 14 centavos (2 cents) and 16 centavos (2 cents), respectively, at 87 centavos (11 cents), 80 centavos (10 cents) and 84 centavos (11 cents), and 1.00 peso (13 cents).
Technical analysts said the bourse was in a consolidation period with no clear trend, and thus subject to speculation.

"The market is in the middle of a consolidation period, with resistance at 3,380 points and support at 3,220 points ... there will be no clear trend as long as it stays within these limits, and speculation can arise over the peso, the Dow Jones, petrochemical privatisation, or whatever," said a technical analyst.
